title: Firmware failure maintenance orchestration runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a draft runbook for SRE and infra teams to coordinate during GPU-level firmware failures that cause node instability, kernel oops, or persistent driver crashes. Focus is cross-team orchestration (SRE, Hardware Ops, Platform Eng), safe cordon/drain, firmware reflash/rollback, temporary capacity reshuffle, and post-incident capture.

Scope / When to use this doc:
- Node(s) showing repeated GPU driver resets, ECC errors, or persistent Xid/UEVENTs across pods after graceful restarts.
- Kernel oops referencing nvme/nvidia or GPU firmware strings.
- Intermittent node flapping leading to degraded cluster capacity and user impact.

High-level goals:
1) Limit customer impact: quick triage and isolated mitigation (cordon/drain, fallback routing).
2) Preserve evidence for postmortem and hardware warranty (collect logs, timestamps, serials).
3) Return nodes to healthy state with minimal risk (safe firmware reflash or hardware swap).
4) Document decisions and handoffs for follow-up (tickets, ownership).

Signals / detection (runbook trigger):
- Alert triggers: repeated driver-reload alerts, node-not-ready with GPU-related taints, elevated pod restarts for inference services.
- Observability checks: per-node token latency spike, GPU utilization drops to 0, nvml errors in logs.
- SRE oncall judgement: if a node fails more than 2 graceful reboots in 24h, start the firmware flow.

Initial triage checklist (0-10 minutes):
- Identify affected nodes (kubectl get nodes -wide; filter by taints/labels).
- Snapshot affected pods: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>.
- Check kernel logs quickly: ssh <node> 'sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver.service -n 200' (or dmesg | tail -n 200).
- Check GPU health: ssh <node> 'nvidia-smi -q' — note persistent errors, ECC counts, Xid entries.
- Note node serial + rack location (asset DB) and take timestamped screenshots/log dumps.
- Set priority channel and CC Hardware/Ops and Platform Eng.

Immediate mitigation (first 15-30 minutes):
- Cordon the node to stop scheduling: kubectl cordon <node>.
- Drain non-critical pods (batch, low-priority jobs) first: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='tier!=critical' --grace-period=60.
- For latency-sensitive pods: if cluster capacity low, shift traffic via routing policy to healthy regions/pools (follow routing runbook).
- If node is flapping and drains fail, escalate to SRE-Shift lead for temporary emergency capacity injection.

Safe reboot vs immediate hardware swap decision tree:
- If logs show a single soft error (Xid 31/43) and node stable after driver unload, attempt a safe reboot and re-evaluate.
- If persistent ECC or firmware mismatch entries or repeated reboots with same errors, escalate to Hardware Ops for hardware-swap.
- If vendor firmware known-bug present (see linked_artifacts), prefer reflash with vendor-approved image under Hardware Ops supervision.

Firmware reflash flow (requires Hardware Ops + Platform Eng):
Pre-reqs (must be done before reflash):
- Take full node dump: /var/log/messages, journalctl -b -1, dmesg, nvidia-smi -q output, lsmod, driver version, bios/fw version (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,firmware_version --format=csv).
- Document serial numbers and open a hardware ticket (JIRA) with attachments.
- Ensure cluster placement: migrate all production-critical pods off node (drain with conservative grace periods).
- Confirm support window with vendor and that firmware image is signed and approved.
- Backup the node boot config and any local artifacts (disk snapshot if necessary).

Reflash steps (high-level):
1) Put node into maintenance mode in inventory, note time and operator.
2) Power-cycle and boot into vendor recovery/USB image per vendor doc (Hardware Ops).
3) Run vendor flashing tool (example: nvflash/fwupd/idiomatic vendor utility).
4) Verify checksum and installed version.
5) Boot node, run nvidia-smi and sanity tests (run a short inference container and run CUDA smoke test).
6) If smoke tests pass, return node to cluster: uncordon after 30m of stable checks.

If reflash fails / hardware swap required:
- Hardware Ops executes physical GPU removal + replacement using hot-swap checklist.
- After component swap, repeat post-swap validation (nvidia-smi, kernel logs).
- If host-level issues remain, collect BMC logs (ipmitool sel list) and escalate to vendor RMA.

Capacity handoff and traffic shaping during remediation:
- If immediate capacity loss > 10%: trigger emergency capacity pool (see infra emergency-capacity playbook).
- Prioritize ML inference lanes: shift highest-priority customer routes to Dedicated pools or other regions with minimal latency impact.
- Update Circuit Breaker and routing hints in Console (whoami: oncall) to avoid retry storms.
- Communicate in #infra-oncall: short status updates every 15 minutes until stable. Use template below.

Verification and safe return criteria (what 'healthy' means):
- Node passes 60-minute rolling health checks: no Xid logs, stable nvidia-smi output, normal kernel logs.
- Scheduler successfully schedules ephemeral load and inference pods without crashes for 2 successive health probes.
- Metrics (GPU errors, pod restarts) back to baseline for 1 hour.
- No customer-facing errors attributable to that node for 2hr.

Rollback and contingency:
- If firmware upgrade causes regressions (higher error rates), rollback to previous vendor firmware per vendor rollback steps.
- If swap fails and capacity still degraded, mark node as DOA and follow RMA flow; update capacity plan and run emergency capacity add.

Communication templates (oncall quick copy):
- Slack initial: "[INC][<node>] Node cordoned for suspected GPU firmware failure. Draining non-critical pods. HW Ops engaged. Impact: X inference routes degraded. ETA: 30m initial triage. CC: @hardware-ops @platform-eng"
- Slack update: "[INC][<node>] Reflash started (vendor image vX.Y). Draining complete. Expected reboot in ~10m. Running smoke tests after boot."
- Pager/StatusPage note (if customer impact): short, factual, avoid speculation.

Post-incident capture (within 24h):
- Attach all collected logs to JIRA ticket.
- Populate postmortem template: timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations implemented, action items with owners and SLAs.
- Create follow-up tasks: firmware rollout plan, automated pre-checks, inventory of nodes with older firmware, telemetry improvements.

Metrics to collect for RCA:
- Per-node GPU error counts over 7d window (ECC, Xid).
- Number of reboots, drain attempts, and pod restarts.
- Time-to-recovery and customer impact delta (requests failed/latency spike).
- Correlate kernel versions and driver versions across affected nodes.

Automation and future work (TODOs):
- Automate firmware version telemetry in Console with alerts for drift > 1 minor version.
- Add a pre-flight health-check job that runs on maintenance window to detect likely failures before flash.
- Draft vendor-approved reflash playbook with exact command snippets and expected outputs (blocked on vendor doc).

Open questions / risks:
- Who has CLI ssh access for reflash in each datacenter? (inventory patching needed)
- Can we run a canary reflash in non-prod racks automatically? (requires infra budget and vendor sign-off)
- Risk: partial reflash that leaves mix of driver/firmware versions — need strict validation steps.

Appendix: quick commands (ops reference)
- Mark cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- Drain safe: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='tier!=critical' --grace-period=60
- Quick GPU health: sudo nvidia-smi -q | egrep 'Product|FB Memory|ECC|Xid' -A2
- Kernel logs: sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver.service -n 500 || sudo dmesg | tail -n 500
- BMC logs: sudo ipmitool sel list || vendor-specific BMC UI

Notes to self / rough timeline example for a 90-minute incident:
- 00:00 Alert fires, oncall acknowledges, cordon + drain started (00:03).
- 00:10 Initial logs captured, HW Ops paged, decision to attempt safe reboot.
- 00:22 Reboot shows repeated errors -> escalate to reflash.
- 00:35 Reflash completed, booting (00:41).
- 00:45 Smoke tests pass, uncordon after 30m of stable checks (01:15).
- 01:30 Incident marked stable; post-incident capture kickoff.

Local TODOs for this document (draft):
- Add vendor-specific reflash commands (pending vendor approval).
- Wire into Console runbooks and copy this flow into the infra runbook index.
- Get Hardware Ops signoff and test the flow in staging rack.

End of draft.

-- Rina K. (SRE)
